newsitem.title: USA: Great Western disagrees with ISS backing.
newsitem.headline: Great Western disagrees with ISS backing.

text.p: Great Western Financial Corp said it vigorously disagreed with Institutional Shareholder Services' (ISS) backing of four out of five of H.F. Ahmanson and Co's consent solicitation proposals.

Earlier, ISS, an advisor to institutional shareholders, said it endorsed four Ahmanson proposals, including one that urges Great Western to open merger discussions with Ahmanson. It said that, as ISS made clear, its recommendations pertain only to Ahmanson's proposed resolutions and bi-law amendments and not on the merits of the Great Western/ Washington Mutual Inc merger and Ahmanson's unsolicited bid,
Great Western said it remains strongly committed to its merger agreement with Washington Mutual and is working with Washington Mutual's board to move forward with the deal.
It also said it continues to urge all Great Western stockholders to oppose Ahmanson's consent solicitation.
A self-imposed March 27 deadline for the consent passed and shareholders have until about May 12 to respond.
"We anticipate that our stockholders will similarly ignore any other artificial deadlines which Ahmanson may seek to impose," said Great Western in a statement.
A representative for one of Great Western's institutional investors said he was not surprised by ISS's recommendations.
"This consent vote has to do with opening up the discussions and I can't imagine an investor voting against that. It's just common sense," the representative said.
Thomas O'Donnell, analyst with Smith Barney, said the marketplace, rather than the consent solicitation, will determine the final outcome of the deal.
The value of both proposals are based on the value of their stocks.
"The deal will be determined in the marketplace. If Ahmanson has a bigger premium than Washington Mutual, the deal will go to Ahmanson or visa-versa," he said.
